note: First fit, from thimble-master.png; not yet seen on the Quest. Pixels at the parts' own size, relative to the point between Thimble's feet. Pivot is a percentage of the part. Higher z sits in front. Parts are cut from thimble-parts-sheet.png and drawn at scale 0.574; heads from thimble-heads-sheet.png at 1, because the master's head is about 1.5 times the body's paint scale. legs.png is both legs placed as the master stands, with the feet level; the socks sit behind the belly. tail.png is the sheet's tail turned 100 degrees so it runs back from the hip. The rest pose has both arms hanging; the master's paws-clasped pose is acting, not rig. Head offsets are measured: each head is registered on the forward head by its nose and eyes (profile by its thimble brim and eye height).
rules: The head turns and tilts from the chin. Keep its slide small, or it comes off the collar.
Every head's neck is cut on the same curve, so it ends on the front rib of the collar. Re-cut it if a head is repainted.
A soft shadow under the chin seats the head in the collar.
armBack stays behind the body and does not act. arm is the near arm: it raises, examines and holds.
The blink head's face sits 13 px lower in its outline than the forward head's, so the thimble and ears rise a little on a blink while the eyes and nose stay put.
